items.title: Synchronization input can disclose subject data to other local users

findings.title: Synchronization input can disclose subject data to other local users
findings.evidence:
os.makedirs(dirname, exist_ok=True)
    fd, tmpname = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=dirname, prefix=".tmp_", suffix=".json")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
        os.chmod(tmpname, 0o644)
        os.replace(tmpname, fname)
findings.explanation: On a shared POSIX computer, when the home directory and newly created sync directory are traversable by other users, mode 0644 lets those users read the input JSON. BuildInput includes anatomical and segmentation paths, trajectory names and positions, which may contain identifiers or sensitive subject information; chmod also overrides a restrictive umask for the file.
findings.suggestion: Create or validate the sync directory as private and keep synchronization files owner-readable and writable only, ensuring the same-user BabelBrain process can still access them.

claude.reason: SyncProtocol.py:196-201 does chmod 0o644 on the JSON in ~/.BabelBrainSync (line 39). It contains file paths, trajectory names and positions. Other local users could read it only if the home directory is traversable. This is a local, low-sensitivity, minor hardening issue and not a concrete path to harm. 0600 would be better.

gpt.reason: BabelBrain/BabelBrainLib/SyncProtocol.py:198-201 explicitly writes the JSON then sets world-readable permissions: `json.dump(data, f, indent=2)` and `os.chmod(tmpname, 0o644)`. Lines 182-188 include absolute anatomical and segmentation paths and trajectory names and positions; BabelBrain/BabelBrain.py:610-618 calls this for the sync input. If parent directories are traversable by other local users, sensitive metadata is exposed despite a restrictive file umask. Use owner-only permissions, including a private sync directory.

gemini.reason: Checked BabelBrain/BabelBrainLib/SyncProtocol.py:192-201 and 39-40. WriteJSONAtomic uses tempfile.mkstemp (which creates files with 0600 permissions) and then explicitly calls os.chmod(tmpname, 0o644) before replacing ~/.BabelBrainSync/BabelBrainInput.json. This overrides the user's umask and makes the file containing anatomical/segmentation paths and trajectory names world-readable if the user's home directory and ~/.BabelBrainSync are traversable. However, since modern Linux distros/macOS typically restrict home directory traversal or this is only file path/trajectory metadata in a user's home directory, this is a minor hardening suggestion (either omit chmod or use 0o600 / chmod 0o700 on SYNC_PATH), not a blocking issue.

items.title: T1 export can overwrite an existing image without confirmation

findings.title: T1 export can overwrite an existing image without confirmation
findings.evidence:
if header is None or header["affine"] is None:
            name = SP.MakeTargetNames([volumeNode.GetName()])[0]
            fname = os.path.join(outputPath, name + "_T1w.nii.gz")
            slicer.util.exportNode(volumeNode, fname)
            header = SP.ReadNiftiHeader(fname)
findings.explanation: When a modified volume or non-NIfTI input is run, the extension exports it to a predictable name in the selected output directory without checking whether that file already exists. An existing image at that path, potentially another subject's scan or an earlier version, can be overwritten before the later warning is shown.
findings.suggestion: Use a unique filename or explicitly check for an existing destination and obtain informed confirmation before replacing it.

claude.reason: BabelBrain.py:554-558 exports the volume to <outputPath>/<name>_T1w.nii.gz without an existence check. The directory is user-chosen and the file name is derived from the volume, so the file is the extension's own artifact. Overwriting it is a normal behavior and a minor bug. The code warns the user about the saved path (559-560). It is not a safety blocker.

gpt.reason: BabelBrain/BabelBrain.py:548-560 chooses export for modified, non-NIfTI, or unsuitable-header inputs and calls `slicer.util.exportNode(volumeNode, fname)` at a predictable `<sanitized node name>_T1w.nii.gz` path with no existing-file check or confirmation. The warning is only shown after launch returns (lines 369-377), so a collision can destroy a previous image before notification. Avoid collisions or obtain confirmation before writing. Slicer's export implementation is external to this checkout and was not independently inspected or run.

gemini.reason: Checked BabelBrain/BabelBrain.py:534-563. When the volume node is not backed by an unmodified NIfTI file with a valid affine, prepareAnatomicalVolume exports it to os.path.join(outputPath, name + '_T1w.nii.gz') via slicer.util.exportNode(volumeNode, fname) without checking if that file already exists, and sets exported = fname so the informational message is shown afterward (lines 285-290). Writing derived outputs to a user-selected output directory with a deterministic name (`<VolumeName>_T1w.nii.gz`) is standard behavior in scientific/medical imaging workflows, though checking for existing files or warning before overwriting would be a nice minor UX improvement.

items.title: Geometry mismatch warning is shown only after launching BabelBrain

findings.title: Geometry mismatch warning is shown only after launching BabelBrain
findings.explanation: prepareT1w reports an affine mismatch that may misplace trajectories, but launch starts the external process before returning that warning. Users cannot review or cancel the mismatch before the application receives the inputs.
findings.suggestion: Validate geometry and present warnings before starting the external application, with an option to cancel.

items.title: Stale output JSON can be loaded as results of a new session

findings.title: Stale output JSON can be loaded as results of a new session
findings.evidence:

findings.explanation: findOutputFile only checks whether ~/.BabelBrainSync/BabelBrainOutput.json exists. The file is deleted only at launch, so before the next Run the Load button can load an old or unrelated session's results (including maps and _mod transforms from other trajectories).
findings.suggestion: Enable loading only for the current session, or show the file's timestamp and createdBy.

items.title: Catalog entry tracks a moving branch

findings.title: Catalog entry tracks a moving branch
findings.explanation: scm_revision is "main", so the built source can change without a catalog update. Branch references are permitted, but the reviewed commit (a3c72bf) is not what is pinned.
findings.suggestion: Optionally pin scm_revision to a commit hash or tag.

items.title: Module category differs from extension category

findings.title: Module category differs from extension category
findings.explanation: The module sets "Focused Ultrasound" while the extension's CMake and catalog category is "Ultrasound". This is cosmetic.

items.title: Result image paths from JSON are loaded without validation

findings.title: Result image paths from JSON are loaded without validation
findings.explanation: Image paths in BabelBrainOutput.json are passed to slicer.util.loadVolume. The file lives in the user's home directory, so there is no privilege boundary. A tampered file could only make Slicer load arbitrary volume files.
findings.suggestion: Optionally restrict loading to .nii/.nii.gz files under the output directory.
